rationale: Start with a broad, strong scouting gradient at moderate temperature to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute and to reveal the overall retention window and any severe crowding. This gives a useful first map without being excessively long.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the fastest path to a higher CRF is to reduce analysis time while keeping the same wide gradient window. Shortening tG by one step should pull the last peak earlier with a good chance of preserving resolution.

The limiting pair is now just above the 1.5 threshold, but there is still slight time penalty left, so one more reduction in gradient time is the most efficient probe. This tests whether we can get t_last under 10 min while staying resolved, with a close fallback if the critical pair breaks.

At 14 min the critical pair lost resolution, so recover selectivity by increasing temperature one step while keeping the faster 16 min gradient. This may push the last peak below 10 min and maintain or improve the borderline 6/7 separation.

Temperature hurt the critical 6/7 pair, so keep 40 C and instead narrow the gradient window slightly at the high end to flatten the effective slope in the region where the late-cluster elutes. This should improve the borderline separation while potentially keeping the run near the 10 min target.

Since tG must stay on the 2 min grid, test a slightly higher starting strength to trim overall retention while keeping the successful 16 min, 40 C conditions. This may bring the last peak under 10 min with less damage to the critical 6/7 pair than the 14 min gradient did.

The higher starting composition improved CRF substantially without losing full resolution, so take one more step in the same direction to try to push the last peak just under 10 min. The critical pair still has some resolution margin at 1.64, making this a strong optimization move.

You already have the maximum CRF, so the only worthwhile move is to see whether the method can be made even faster while staying fully resolved. Raising phi0 one more step is the most direct test, and if the critical pair drops below 1.5 you can revert to injection 7 as the optimum.

Phi0 0.15 at 16 min is the current optimum, so the next informative boundary test is whether a shorter 14 min gradient can still keep the 6/7 pair at or above 1.5 at this stronger start. If it succeeds, it would also score 1.000 with a shorter run; if not, injection 7 remains best.

With phi0 0.15 and tG 16 already perfect, test a slightly lower phi1 to flatten the gradient around the critical late cluster while keeping the same start strength. This checks whether full resolution can be retained with a comparable sub-10 min last peak, potentially giving a more robust optimum around the 6/7 pair.

Lowering phi1 to 0.90 improved the critical-pair margin but only barely missed the 10 min target, so one more step lower is a good robustness probe. This tests whether extra selectivity for the 6/7 pair can be gained without sacrificing the perfect score region too much.

Injection 7 is optimal on score, so now probe robustness from the other selectivity axis by lowering temperature one step while keeping the winning gradient. This checks whether the critical 6/7 pair gains margin without pushing the last peak past 10 min too severely.

Since 16 min at 40 C is perfect and both shorter tG and altered T degrade resolution, the remaining useful check is a slightly longer gradient at the same phi window to see if it gives extra robustness and whether the 6/7 pair is indeed the limiting boundary. This should map the local optimum around the winning method without risking truncation.

Temperature changes appear to swap selectivity among the middle peaks, so a second step lower than 35 C is informative for mapping that behavior around the winning method. This tests whether the 5/6 issue seen at 35 C strengthens further or whether a different useful selectivity region emerges.

The best score is already achieved, so use remaining budget to map nearby robust alternatives by combining the two single changes that individually improved the critical-pair margin: lower phi0 than the optimum and lower phi1 than the optimum. This should show whether a flatter, slightly wider-retention method can retain full resolution close to the 10 min boundary.

The optimum is already identified, so use remaining runs to bracket temperature behavior above 45 C at the winning gradient. This will confirm whether higher temperature consistently worsens the critical selectivity and helps define the robustness limits around the best method.

Continue the temperature bracketing one final step above the optimum to complete the local selectivity map at fixed gradient conditions. This will confirm the monotonic deterioration of the critical pair with increasing temperature and fully define the robustness boundary.

One final temperature point completes the full allowed temperature map around the winning method. This will show whether the selectivity crossover continues above 55 C and firmly establish 40 C as the best operating point.

The optimum is secure, so use remaining budget to test a more compressed gradient window at the winning phi0 and temperature. This checks whether stronger flattening of the late-region slope can preserve full resolution with an acceptable time, extending the robustness map on the phi1 axis.

Map the remaining unexplored corner nearest the optimum by combining the modestly safer phi0 0.10 with the shorter 14 min gradient. This tests whether the extra resolution margin from lower phi0 is enough to keep the critical pair resolved under the faster gradient.

Use the remaining budget to bracket the short-gradient limit at the gentlest start composition, which has given the strongest critical-pair resolution margin. This tests whether the additional reduction in tG causes only the known 6/7 pair to fail or reveals a sharper collapse elsewhere.

Probe the high-phi0 boundary one more step beyond the failed 0.20 start to define how sharply the critical-pair resolution collapses as run time shortens. This completes the local phi0 map around the optimum and confirms the usable upper limit.

One remaining useful map point is to continue lowering phi1 at the winning phi0 to see how far the gain in critical-pair resolution extends before time becomes prohibitive. This defines the low-phi1 boundary around the optimum more completely.

With two runs left and the optimum already found, test a combined flatter-and-faster condition that has not yet been explored: lower phi1 to gain local selectivity while using the shorter 14 min gradient and safer phi0 0.10. This helps determine whether the 14 min failure can be rescued by narrowing the gradient window rather than by changing temperature.

Injection 24 reached the maximum score at the faster 14 min gradient, so the last run should test whether one more step lower in phi1 preserves full resolution while pulling the last peak just under 10 min. If successful, this would give an equally perfect but slightly more robust short-gradient optimum.
